headline: Check Tide Times Before Crossing the Causeway
reservation: Entry to the castle and island does not require a regional permit, but access is strictly governed by the North Sea tides. Visitors must consult official Northumberland County Council safe crossing times for the road causeway; accommodation or castle tickets should be verified against these windows.

days.title: Castles and Causeway Crossings

stops.name: Lindisfarne Castle
stops.detail: Explore the centuries-old history and 19th-century lime kilns via a one-mile walk from the visitor car park. Visit the walled garden designed by Gertrude Jekyll located near the castle headland.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes from the A1; total travel time depends entirely on tidal windows.
days.note: The castle is accessed by a steep cobbled ramp and steps; sturdy footwear is recommended for the terrain.

intel.title: Tidal Causeway Hazards
intel.text: The only road access is a three-mile causeway covered twice daily by the tide. Always check safe crossing times and allow an extra 30 minutes for weather variables like high winds.

intel.title: Walking the Sands
intel.text: The marked walking route over mud and sands has different safety requirements than the road. Never cross during a rising tide and aim to finish the walk before the mid-point of the safe road crossing window.

intel.title: Visitor Parking
intel.text: A visitor car park is situated one mile from the castle entrance. A drop-off point exists outside the gate for those with limited mobility.

intel.title: Supplies and Fuel
intel.text: The island is small with limited facilities; verify fuel and specific supply locations on the mainland before crossing. Evidence does not specify fuel stations on the island.

intel.title: Connectivity Status
intel.text: Specific signal coverage for the island is not detailed in current official sources. Ensure you have downloaded tidal charts offline before reaching the causeway.

plan.arrival: Exit the A1 and travel five miles east to the causeway. Verify the tide is out before attempting the three-mile drive to the island car park.
plan.vehicle: Cars are the most common way to visit; check rental restrictions regarding driving on tidal-affected roads.
plan.goldenHour: Castle headland for sunset, subject to tidal road closure times.
